race_context: The office is the board of Lewis Cass Schools, based in Walton in southeastern Cass County (100 S. Main St., Walton) {lc_trustees}{lc_supt}. State records list the corporation as Southeastern School Corp. through 2017 and as Lewis Cass Schools since 2018 {idoe_enroll}. State enrollment counts were 1,293 students in 2023-24, 1,283 in 2024-25 and 1,279 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.

Superintendent: Tim Shoaff, a 1997 Lewis Cass graduate who spent the previous 13 years at Northwestern High School in Kokomo as assistant principal and then principal, started in July 2026. He is the fourth superintendent since 2024: Tim Garland resigned in April 2024 after nearly 10 years, Steve Darnell served as interim through 2024, and Chris Daughtry led the district for about 18 months before leaving for Wabash City Schools {pt_shoaff_hired}. Shoaff said his priorities include better communication with parents, including around the new state ban on student cell phones in schools {pt_shoaff_profile}.

Board: the district website lists five board members: Tim Johnson (president), Becky Comoglio (vice president), Ryan Zeck (secretary), Rick Lee and Kristi Hull {lc_trustees}. Members have been elected to five numbered districts, one member each, with every district race on the ballot in every Lewis Cass precinct and a residency requirement tied to township {lc_vacancy_2022}{cass_2022}{cass_2024}. In 2022 Kristi Hull won District 3 (635 votes to 601 for Robert S. McLaughlin, 560 for Brian Thomas and 393 for Jeffrey A. Packard) and Ryan Zeck was unopposed in District 4; in 2024 Becky Comoglio was unopposed in District 1 and Tim Johnson beat Rick Lee in District 5, 1,680 to 1,523 {cass_2022}{cass_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: two seats, each 'vote for one,' matching the state list: 'Lewis Cass School Board District 2 At Large' (Mark W Chambers and Lucas R. Shideler) and 'Lewis Cass School Board District 2' (Maggie Hintz, Kristi Hull and Ryne D. Stover) {cass_ballot_miami}{cass_ballot_walton}{in_list}. Both contests appear on ballots across the district's precincts {cass_ballot_miami}{cass_ballot_walton}{cass_ballot_deercreek}. The seats up are the ones filled in 2022 (Hull's District 3 seat and Zeck's District 4 seat) {cass_2022}; the ballot labels differ from the old district numbers, and this guide could not find a public explanation of the new seat structure. Hull, a current board member, is running; Zeck is not on the ballot {lc_trustees}{cass_ballot_walton}.

Budget: in February 2025, then-superintendent Chris Daughtry said nearly all of the district's Debt Service Fund and just under half of its Operations Fund come from property taxes, and that 'further property tax losses prevent schools from being able to maintain their facilities and provide a safe and adequate learning environment for students' {pt_sb1_2025}. This guide found no later reporting on how the final 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Lewis Cass, and no operating or safety referendum.

Programs and grants: Starting in fall 2025, Lewis Cass High School partnered with IU Kokomo to offer Indiana College Core classes for college credit {pt_college_core}. In May 2026 the Logansport Redevelopment Commission approved $41,443 to upgrade the high school's culinary pathway classroom {pt_culinary}. In September 2026 the state awarded Lewis Cass Schools a $27,950 Secured School Safety grant {pt_safety}.

Forums: the League of Women Voters of Cass County and the Logansport/Cass County Chamber of Commerce invited candidates in both Lewis Cass board races to a Sept. 29, 2026 debate {pt_debate_set}. The Pharos-Tribune's report on the event covered four offices (county council, Eel Township trustee, sheriff and state representative) and did not mention the school board races {pt_debate}. This guide found no candidate questionnaire, website or campaign page for any Lewis Cass candidate.
